item.content:encoded:
One hundred women from seven villages across Vava'u are taking part in a capacity-building programme, under the Reef to Ridge Phase 2 program, aimed at strengthening sustainable livelihoods, preserving traditional knowledge and supporting environmental protection.

The initiative, launched by UNDP in partnership with Langafanoa 'a Fafine or National Women's Council Tonga, supported by HRH Crown Princess Sinaitakala Tuku'aho, focuses on expanding economic opportunities for local women entrepreneurs while promoting climate resilience and environmental stewardship.

Over the coming days, participants will develop skills in quality handicrafts and weaving, with the programme designed to help women improve the value and marketability of traditional crafts.

The programme also provides participants with business skills to support their economic independence, while promoting women-led approaches to waste management and the protection of marine and terrestrial environments.

UNDP Programme Specialist Merewalesi Laveti and MEIDECC CEO Sione Akau'ola attended the launch, marking another milestone under the joint UNDP and MEIDECC Ridge to Reef programme.

Organisers said the initiative also aimed to preserve traditional ecological knowledge by creating opportunities for younger women to learn skills and knowledge passed down through generations. They said linking traditional knowledge with new livelihood and environmental approaches would help support the long-term sustainable development of Vava'u.

The programme recognises women as key contributors to environmental protection and economic resilience, with the initiative seeking to strengthen their capacity to lead sustainable solutions within their communities.

item.title: Secondary students quizzed on climate change
item.description: Secondary school students across Tongatapu have begun competing in a climate change quiz aimed at strengthening youth awareness, academic knowledge and understanding of the impacts of climate change on Tonga and the wider Pacific. The competition on Friday, 21 August 2026 brings together Form 5 students from eight registered secondary schools across Tongatapu.
item.content:encoded:
Secondary school students across Tongatapu have begun competing in a climate change quiz aimed at strengthening youth awareness, academic knowledge and understanding of the impacts of climate change on Tonga and the wider Pacific.

The competition on Friday, 21 August 2026 brings together Form 5 students from eight registered secondary schools across Tongatapu.

CEO for MEIDECC , Sione ‘Akau‘ola, said the initiative was important in strengthening climate change awareness among young people.

He also highlighted the educational benefits of the competition, saying it provided students with an opportunity to revise and strengthen their knowledge ahead of their final examinations.

He hoped future competitions could expand beyond Tongatapu to include secondary schools in Vava‘u, Ha‘apai, ‘Eua and the Niuas.

Principal of newly established Anastasis College, Momea Tu‘ifua, on behalf of the Principals’ Association expressed support for the competition. She said initiatives that complemented classroom learning were valuable in strengthening students’ understanding of climate change and its relevance to Tonga's future.

Each match consists of three rounds and 35 questions covering academic subjects, technical climate change knowledge and current events.

The first round has 15 questions from Science, Biology and Geography, while the second includes 10 technical questions focused specifically on climate change.

The final round consists of 10 questions covering climate change current events and general knowledge.

The opening round of matches saw Tonga High School defeat Queen Salote College, while Tupou College secured victory over Takuilau College.

Ocean of Light International School defeated Tonga College ‘Atele, and Liahona High School won against Anastasis College.

The competition will continue next Friday as schools progress towards the final, which will form part of National Climate Change Awareness Week 2026.

The Tongatapu Secondary Schools Climate Change Quiz Competition launched by the Department of Climate Change within the Ministry of Meteorology, Energy, Information, Disaster Management, Environment, Climate Change and Communications ( MEIDECC ) as part of preparations for National Climate Change Awareness Week next month.
